subject: Seasonal SLA metering & discounting mechanism proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Seasonal SLA metering & discounting — initial proposal

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our discussion about BrightGrid's seasonal usage spikes (Q4 marketing windows and year-end batch runs), we put together a short proposal for how Redwood can structure SLA metering and discounts to align cost predictability with your operational peaks.

High-level idea:
- Base commit: standard uptime tier (99.9%) and response SLA; billed monthly at agreed committed capacity.
- Seasonal metering windows: defined 3-month peak periods where BrightGrid can declare an elevated committed capacity band. During the window: overage rates are reduced and you receive a one-time seasonal discount on the incremental commit.
- Protective fallback: if actual usage exceeds the elevated band, standard overage pricing applies to protect shared capacity.

Example (draft numbers):
- Base commit: 100 GPU-hours / month at $X/unit.
- Seasonal window (Nov–Jan): declare +30% (130 GPU-hours) for three months; Redwood offers a 10% discount on the incremental 30 GPU-hours for that period.

Attached: sla-pricing-matrix.xlsx (worked examples and band math).

Requests:
1) Can you confirm the months you want designated as seasonal windows?
2) Would BrightGrid prefer fixed seasonal capacity (you pick the increment upfront) or an on-demand declared window each season?

If this looks reasonable I can loop in Legal (Marissa) for contract language and Jordan for operational runbook notes.

Best,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Alice Park <alice@brightgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightgrid.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Seasonal SLA metering & discounting — initial proposal

Hi Karthik —

Thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers:
- Seasonal months: Nov, Dec, Jan are the primary peaks for us. We also have a smaller June spike (campaign-driven) that might be worth treating as a micro-window.
- We prefer the declared-window model where we lock in an elevated capacity 2–3 weeks before the season starts (gives ops time to provision).

Two requests from procurement:
1) Can you show the net TCV impact if we take the seasonal incremental commit vs. a pure on-demand overage model? (procurement wants to see line-itemed TCV over 12 months).
2) Any flexibility on the discount if we commit to a multi-year seasonal band? They asked whether the 10% could step to 12% if we commit for 2 seasons/year for two years.

Also, curious about the SLA side — if we elevate committed capacity for the seasonal window, does the response-time SLA change (e.g., faster triage for priority incidents during the window)?

Appreciate the worked examples in the attachment — procurement will review and follow up.

Best,
Alice
Head of Cloud Ops, BrightGrid
alice@brightgrid.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@brightgrid.com>, procurement@brightgrid.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Seasonal SLA metering & discounting — initial proposal

Alice — thanks, noted. Quick responses below and attached a revised matrix with TCV scenarios.

Short answers:
- TCV: See tab "12m-TCV-comparison" in sla-pricing-matrix.xlsx. We modeled three cases: no seasonal commit (pure overage), single-season commit (3 months), and multi-year seasonal commit. The committed-season case smooths spend and reduces volatility; multi-year commitment yields additional discounting tiers.
- Multi-year ramp: we can tier the seasonal incremental discount as follows: 10% (1 season commit), 12% (2 seasons/year for 2 years), 15% (multi-year pilot with guaranteed minimum growth). We can bake that into an appendix.
- Response SLA during seasonal windows: operationally we can offer a covered priority response path for incidents declared as "seasonal-impacting" — effectively a higher-priority triage with the same uptime commitment. That means:
  * Priority triage: 30-minute initial response for P1s (vs standard 60-minute) during declared windows.
  * Dedicated escalation contact during window (named on-call rotation).

Trade-offs: the stepped response time and dedicated escalations are operational commitments from Redwood and therefore map to the discount tiers above (they increase cost on our side). We can quantify run-rate headcount coverage in the TCV tab.

Action items:
- Alice/procurement: confirm the exact seasonal months and whether you prefer the 2-week declaration or a fixed auto-enroll for the same months each year.
- Marissa: can you draft a short contract appendix that covers seasonal band declarations, discount ladder, and the priority triage addendum?
- Jordan: please add a short runbook sketch for the named escalation and triage flow.

Attaching: sla-pricing-matrix.xlsx (updated) and contract-draft-v2.docx (placeholder with appendix section).

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@brightgrid.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightgrid.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Seasonal SLA metering & discounting — initial proposal

Hi Alice / team —

I reviewed Karthik's wording and the updated matrix. Drafting note for procurement:
- Appendix language will include: definition of "Seasonal Window" (start/end dates or calendar months), declaration timeline (recommended 14 days prior), rollback clause (once declared, changes allowed up to 7 days before window start), and discount ladder table.
- Escalation & reporting: we will commit to named escalation contacts and monthly usage reconciliations during windows. We will also add a mid-window checkpoint (reporting + opportunity to top-up commit if both parties agree).
- Risk & termination: multi-year seasonal commitments will include a usage true-up and an early-termination carve-out for force majeure.

I will put a redline together by Friday and share. Jordan — if you can draft the 1-page ops runbook for the named escalation and priority triage (who responds, SLAs, communication channels), I will attach it as an annex to the appendix.

Alice — if procurement confirms the preference for a 2-year multi-season commitment at the 12% level, we can run the pricing math and present a final commercial offer next week.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
